rationale: Round 1 built and passed cleanly, so this table raises aggression on control-flow hiding while protecting the hot recursive core (Towers/Move/tower) via moderately elevated RuntimeCost on BCF and FLA, letting the feature-driven selector steer the most invasive passes toward cold functions (Init, Oscar-era helpers, Queens/Quicksort wrappers). SUB stays near-free and high-gain since arithmetic mixing is the cheapest per-instruction resistance for a 1471-byte text footprint; IBR is kept cheap-cost/high-gain to interleave blocks cheaply without inflating the binary. ICALL carries a mid RuntimeCost because indirect dispatch hurts small recursive callers, but its security payoff for defeating static call-graph recovery justifies selective application. IGV gets the highest DiversityGain since it is a compile-time-only transform that diversifies global layout at zero runtime price — ideal for such a tiny program. CorrectnessRisk is kept low everywhere (max 0.25 on FLA) since the prior round showed no ICE or miscompilation, allowing the selector to apply FLA broadly; SPLIT remains a low-cost diversity booster applied wherever basic blocks are large enough. Overall: strong obfuscation, bounded overhead on the recursive hot path, correctness preserved.
